subChunks.title: Capstone — Schema Design and Multi-table Queries
subChunks.hookHtml: The Guild needs a complete database schema and a set of queries. This capstone tests your ability to design tables, write multi-table queries, handle NULLs, and use transactions.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
What this capstone covers

You will design a relational schema and write a set of queries that combine: JOINs (INNER, LEFT), subqueries, GROUP BY, HAVING, CASE WHEN, COALESCE, and transactions.

The scenario

The Guild manages three core entities: members (like apprentices), projects (like quests), and assignments (a member is assigned to a project with a role and start date). Design the schema with proper types, constraints, and foreign keys, then answer the queries below.

Schema design checklist

  • Every table has a primary key
  • Foreign keys are declared with appropriate ON DELETE behaviour
  • NOT NULL on required columns
  • CHECK or ENUM on constrained values
  • Timestamps use TEXT in YYYY-MM-DD format (SQLite) or TIMESTAMP in PostgreSQL

storyBeats.text: The Headmaster places a blank slate before you. 'Design the schema for the Guild Registry from scratch. Then prove it works.'

storyBeats.speaker: Cipher the Archivist
storyBeats.text: Design first. Ask: what entities exist, what are their attributes, what are the relationships? One-to-many or many-to-many? Then write CREATE TABLE. Then write INSERT to populate. Then write the queries. Every step is tested by the next.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
🎓 Guild Registry Schema

Design and CREATE the following tables with proper constraints:

  1. members: id (PK), name (NOT NULL), role (NOT NULL, CHECK IN Apprentice/Senior/Lead), xp (NOT NULL, DEFAULT 0, CHECK >= 0), joined_at (TEXT NOT NULL)
  2. projects: id (PK), title (NOT NULL UNIQUE), status (NOT NULL, CHECK IN active/completed/archived), created_at (TEXT NOT NULL)
  3. assignments: id (PK), member_id (FK → members ON DELETE CASCADE), project_id (FK → projects ON DELETE RESTRICT), assigned_role (TEXT NOT NULL), started_at (TEXT NOT NULL)

Then write these queries against sample data of your choice:

  • All members with their assignment count (0 if unassigned)
  • Projects with their total member XP (sum of assigned members' xp)
  • Members with XP above the average for their role
subChunks.guidedPracticeModelAnswer:
-- Schema:
CREATE TABLE members (
  id        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name      TEXT    NOT NULL,
  role      TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('Apprentice','Senior','Lead')),
  xp        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (xp >= 0),
  joined_at TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE projects (
  id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  title      TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  status     TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('active','completed','archived')),
  created_at TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE assignments (
  id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  member_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  project_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  assigned_role TEXT   NOT NULL,
  started_at   TEXT    NOT NULL
);

-- Query 1: assignment count per member (LEFT JOIN to include unassigned)
SELECT m.name, COUNT(a.id) AS assignment_count
FROM   members AS m
LEFT JOIN assignments AS a ON a.member_id = m.id
GROUP BY m.name
ORDER BY assignment_count DESC;

-- Query 2: total xp per project
SELECT p.title, COALESCE(SUM(m.xp), 0) AS total_xp
FROM   projects AS p
LEFT JOIN assignments AS a ON a.project_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN members     AS m ON m.id = a.member_id
GROUP BY p.title
ORDER BY total_xp DESC;

-- Query 3: above-average xp within role (correlated subquery)
SELECT m.name, m.role, m.xp
FROM   members AS m
WHERE  m.xp > (
  SELECT AVG(m2.xp) FROM members AS m2 WHERE m2.role = m.role
)
ORDER BY m.role, m.xp DESC;
subChunks.soloPracticeHtml:
🏹 Solo — Transaction

Write a transaction that reassigns all 'Apprentice' members from a completed project (project status = 'completed') to a new active project. Use BEGIN/COMMIT and describe in comments what you check before committing.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Walk through the process of designing a relational schema for a new use case: how do you identify entities, relationships, and constraints before writing a single CREATE TABLE?

questions.prompt: In the Guild schema, why does assignments.project_id use ON DELETE RESTRICT rather than CASCADE?
options: To prevent deleting a project while assignments still exist — preserving the history of who worked on it
To automatically delete all assignments when a project is deleted
Because RESTRICT is the only option for foreign keys to projects
To set assignments to NULL when a project is deleted
questions.answer: To prevent deleting a project while assignments still exist — preserving the history of who worked on it
questions.explanation: ON DELETE RESTRICT (the default) prevents parent deletion when children exist. Deleting a project with active assignments should require archiving or reassigning those members first — not silently destroying the history.

questions.prompt: The query `SELECT m.name, COUNT(a.id) AS n FROM members LEFT JOIN assignments ... GROUP BY m.name` returns n=0 for some members. What does that mean?
options: Those members have no assignments — LEFT JOIN kept their row with NULL on the right; COUNT(a.id) counts non-NULL id values, returning 0
COUNT(*) would also return 0 for those members
Those members have exactly one assignment
The LEFT JOIN failed for those members
questions.answer: Those members have no assignments — LEFT JOIN kept their row with NULL on the right; COUNT(a.id) counts non-NULL id values, returning 0
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps the member row even with no match. The assignment columns are NULL. COUNT(a.id) counts non-NULL values — 0 for unmatched members. COUNT(*) would count 1 for those rows.

questions.prompt: Which schema design choice prevents inserting a project with status = 'pending' (not in the allowed list)?
options: CHECK (status IN ('active','completed','archived')) on the status column
NOT NULL on the status column
A foreign key referencing a statuses table
questions.answer: CHECK (status IN ('active','completed','archived')) on the status column
questions.explanation: The CHECK constraint enforces a whitelist of allowed values. NOT NULL only prevents NULL — it allows any string. A foreign-key to a statuses table also works and is more flexible when the list grows.

questions.prompt: After completing this capstone, what is the most important habit to carry into every production schema design?
options: Write constraints (NOT NULL, CHECK, FK) at creation time — retrofitting them to a populated table is painful and often breaks existing data
Never use TEXT columns — use VARCHAR with explicit length limits
Keep all tables in a single database schema for simplicity
questions.answer: Write constraints (NOT NULL, CHECK, FK) at creation time — retrofitting them to a populated table is painful and often breaks existing data
questions.explanation: Adding a NOT NULL constraint to a column that already contains NULLs requires a data migration. Adding a foreign key fails if orphaned rows exist. Constraints are far easier to define upfront than to add later to a populated production table.
